## LaporCovid-19

Scores draw on two peer-reviewed articles [@ekawati2022; @rinaldi2024] and the
coalition's own report [@laporcovid2021]. A citizen coalition founded the
initiative, designed the reporting platform, ran the database with volunteers,
analysed and published the data, and advocated for families of health workers,
so every Domain A stage was scored as led (●) and the case is classed as
extreme citizen science. It counted health-worker deaths while no official
figure was published (C1 and C2 = ●). Its contribution to policy on
compensation is self-reported (C3 = ◐), and its current status is not
documented (D1 = NR). Under the verdict rules in S1.4, D1 = NR gives
insufficient evidence; Table S3 and the main text currently list the verdict as
partial [to be reconciled before submission].

- - Item
  - Score
  - Justification

- - A1
  - ●
  - Citizen coalition founded the initiative and set its questions

- - A2
  - ●
  - Coalition designed the reporting platform and database

- - A3
  - ●
  - Volunteers ran the database

- - A4
  - ●
  - Analysis by LaporCovid-19-affiliated authors

- - A5
  - ●
  - Group published articles and commentary

- - A6
  - ●
  - Group advocated for families of health workers

- - B1
  - ●

- - B2
  - NR
  - Return of results to reporters not documented

- - B3
  - ●
  - Aggregated data public; article open access

- - B4
  - ◐
  - Affiliated contributors named as authors; choice of credit not documented

- - B5
  - ●

- - B6

- - B7

- - C1
  - ●

- - C2

- - C3

- - D2

Leadership note: leading roles were held by civil-society experts, journalists and activists; lay members of the public mainly reported data.
